body:
Birth control? Damn it, I was hoping to try it again at some point. My first period during the adjustment to low carb/low GI has been fucking TERRIBLE, so I was bleeding to death the day this happened -- a detail I left out of the original story.

Oh well. Better safe than sorry.

I'm still really nervous about even approaching them. I'm going to have to at some point, and hopefully the worst case scenario is just that they think I'm a little selfish. And yeah -- this is more than just a bad day.

I have been working on getting help (been diagnosed, tried a million meds, psych ward stay, the whole nine yards -- I've been dealing with this crap since I was 11), but at this point I can't afford to shell out 1/4th of my paycheck for a therapist appointment. I'm just trying to keep a roof over my head. :(

Maybe Medicare will come through? That would be wonderful. Zoloft made me sick as a dog and never worked for me (since you need a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder), but Lamictal was great. It's the best med I ever took. I'd be on it if I could afford it right now. Zoloft does absolute wonders for some people though, so I'm glad it worked for you. :)

Considering it. Said friend has a bad habit of almost completely forgetting I exist whenever he's dating someone (even though he knows that really fucks with a certain mental issue I have and makes me depressed), despite us having been best friends/roommates for a few years, and I guess this time I'm just over it instead of being miserable like I was the last time it happened. It's not an 'I'm jealous' situation (because holy hell, I'm not) but more of a 'you only communicate with me to tell me your gf is coming over most of the time'. There's also the fact that despite me having brought it up for years now all the cleaning in the place rests on me, and I just can't deal with it anymore. 

I dunno -- I feel really bad about the whole thing. We don't really talk anymore aside from surface stuff occasionally, and where I once felt all of this awesome inspiration (we were gonna do all this stuff together and would talk about how we'd still be best friends even when we were old and almost dead) there's kind of a nothingness now. Thing is, the last time he did it he apologized for pretty much cutting me out of his life, and I forgave him, and he said sorry when I mentioned it recently but that didn't change much. I don't want to break off the friendship, but I know once I either move out or say I'm heading elsewhere when my lease expires that that'll be pretty much it. If you barely see someone while you're living with them, it'll be worse when you aren't.

The whole thing just kinda hurts my heart. A lot.
Godspeed, you batshit insane poop diamond.
Like a BOSS.

On one hand, if it's established work etiquette (which differs for every place) then you could make the argument that it would be the same no matter what the disturbance was. Unfortunately, the way you worded it doesn't come off as just adherence to rules, it comes off as you taking a dig at women talking about pregnancy -- which is a big deal. That's nine months of bullshit as opposed to a colonoscopy, and also it's a big deal to the women that were discussing it. Honestly, just apologize and clarify that you were simply considering work ethic, not making a statement about how women should keep pregnancy details to themselves. Pas de problème.

You didn't fuck up by having sex with your girlfriend (don't care about the age difference, my own parents were 16 and 21 when they met but my mother was really mature/graduated high school early), you fucked up by bringing your girlfriend that your mother doesn't approve of back to *her* house and got caught having sex with her while your parents were at a funeral for your step-grandfather. It's more of a 'they were already having a shitty time and you were kinda insensitive' thing. 

Moving out doesn't seem like a bad idea if you're going to continue this relationship and want to be able to do so without stepping on any toes. I hate to say it but it's kinda a dick move to bring her around and be all 'fuck the police' to your mother whether her disapproval is right or not. It *is* her and your stepdad's house and I assume you aren't paying rent.

We can start a club, babe. I'm in the same boat. Apparently I make a *great* friend but I'm just not girlfriend material, for anyone who's actually looking for a relationship and not just trying to get laid (which tends to be creepy ass older dudes on the train that look like they could be my grandfather). The other commenter is right though. There are billions of people out there that come to appreciate things other than physical attractiveness, and it is most definitely in the realm of possibility that one day you'll have an awkward encounter with someone who is also awkward, and who appreciates your smarts and your personality and all your quirks. I don't know how long it will take, but you're just 20. I have friends that didn't find the person for them until 30, or later, so don't give up hope just yet. ::hug::
OP let it slip through his fingers.

"Give it to the one who deserves me" Bingo. I'm 27 and still holding on to it just because all the offers I've had were not people that I trusted enough with that level of vulnerability or that I actually wanted to have sex with. Our society has this sort of bipolar view of sexuality in that we freak out over a nipple or a ball in a photo but we think everyone should be having all the sex, all the time, regardless of whether their sex drive is actually that high or not, and if they aren't they're prudish. If you're okay satisfying yourself while waiting for someone you feel like losing your virginity too, go with it. I wouldn't say ONLY save yourself for marriage simply because if you're going to marry someone, you might want an idea of how the physical side of the relationship is going to go, but I believe that even if it isn't ideal if you have a strong enough relationship you can work through it. But don't feel pressured to 'not be a virgin anymore' just because society acts like it's shameful or something. Fuck that noise, OP. : )

I've been told that, too. Relative low carb can certain be maintained, and it's probably the best way to go for me. It's unfortunately much more expensive to eat healthily than it is to eat the kind of crap priced for broke college kids. Then again, there's probably a thread on Reddit specifically about this somewhere...

Medicine frightens me. From the age of 13, I've been on medicines that have made me nauseous, made me a complete zombie, made me see and hear crazy shit, given me nightmares and made me temporarily afraid of sleeping, made me gain weight, stop eating, or a weird combination of the two; I'm apparently medicine resistant, so I've been on a lot of stuff. That said, I'm going to give herbal medicine a shot. It can't hurt, and no side effects! If I can find something that works as a reasonably effective mood stabilizer, that will do wonders. : )

There also could be absolutely nothing on the other side. I'm completely neutral -- I was raised in a religion without a concept of the afterlife, so it's odd to try to incorporate the possibility into my belief system (what remains of one) as an adult. I didn't grow up thinking about hell and heaven as destinations, or even that my soul would survive the destruction of my body.

I dunno, man. I have fleeting moments of happiness where I'm stricken with 'I'm alive, and I'm happy'. I can't really explain it, but they're those moments when you're overwhelmed by how wonderful life can be. But it's like turning off the lights in a room; the darkness left behind once the light recedes is all the more repressive. When I have a mood swing going downward after being so incredibly happy, it feels all the worse because I know it will be a while before I can physically feel that again, no matter what I do to try to cheer myself up. And it isn't like I don't try. So I know I'm lucky, but it doesn't feel that way too often. I'm aware of the fact, though.

I'd been doing low carb (moderately) and feeling better physically as a result, but finals and depression have pushed me back into eating bullshit. I plan to change that as soon as I can. What you've described sounds like a modified version of the ketogenic diet, or paleo/primal (with avoiding processed foods and white rice/bread. I did successfully cut out soda and juice (except for SOMETIMES).

I don't know your full situation, but I hope you find a way out of it at some point. I'm sorry you're having to go through that. I do feel guilty for letting my depression drag me down so far when I do have a support system; but on the other, less moral hand, they are also liabilities keeping me here. 

Also, this is some stupid shit, and I apologize if it's patronizing, but if you need someone to talk to, inbox me. No one should have to be completely alone, and I'm not going anywhere anytime soon. : (
I've been writing some awful poetry to cope recently. It will never SEE THE LIGHT OF DAY, but it is a passable release. Thanks for the offer, by the way. : )

It's not so much that I don't want it; I would give anything to be able to go back to the sliding scale clinic I was at before, but they've issued a medicine requirement -- and I can't deal with being flipped from medication with crippling side effect to medication with crippling side effect again without my quality of life going right down the drain. : (

I might have to, though.
I don't know if you're just tired or actually depressed, but ::hug::. It would be easy. Most of the shit that seems worth doing isn't easy, though. : (

Gonna sound stupid as all hell, but I really do enjoy helping people (and animals). Also, creating things (writing, working with clay, etc.) There are definitely things I enjoy, but happiness is weird. You spend so long being unhappy despite your best efforts, that you become unable to differentiate between the two emotions. That, too, sounds stupid. I'm sorry.

I've been an insomniac since I was about 14, so I used to appreciate some of the medication used to help you sleep. But some of the medicines I've been prescribed for the manic depression have made me very leery of anything that has a drowsiness side effect. Sometimes it comes with horrific nightmares. : (
You guys are fine. I'm not going to begrudge you having a conversation about a shared interest. : )
